member.name: T:GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.Advanced.DesignerForm
member.summary: Represents the main form of the Flat Designer within the ActiveReports environment. This form serves as the central user interface for designing reports, providing access to various design tools, properties, and settings.
member.remarks: The is a key component of the ActiveReports designer, integrating different functionalities such as the toolbox, property grid, report explorer, and preview capabilities. It also manages sessions and settings to enhance the user experience.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.Advanced.DesignerForm.DesignerTitle
member.summary: Gets or sets a value representing the title of the designer form.
member.value: A that represents the title displayed in the form's title bar.
member.remarks: Setting this property updates the title of the designer form dynamically based on the current report being edited. It also triggers an update to the report name displayed in the file panel, ensuring that the user interface reflects the current state of the report being designed.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.Advanced.DesignerForm.SessionSettingsStorage
member.summary: Gets or sets a value representing the storage mechanism for session settings within the designer form.
member.value: The storage mechanism that implements interface. This property allows for the persistence and retrieval of user session settings, such as tool window positions, recent files list, and other customizable settings of the designer environment.
member.remarks: The session settings storage is crucial for maintaining a consistent user experience across sessions by saving and restoring the state of the designer form based on the user's preferences and actions.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.Advanced.DesignerForm.ExportViewerFactory
member.summary: Gets or sets a value representing the factory responsible for creating export viewers.
member.value: The factory that implements interface. This property is used to generate export viewers that facilitate the export of reports to different formats, enhancing the report sharing and distribution capabilities.
member.remarks: The export viewer factory plays a crucial role in the report export functionality, allowing users to preview and export reports in various formats. It ensures that the appropriate export viewer is used based on the selected export format.

member.name: M:GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.Advanced.DesignerForm.#ctor
member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class.
member.remarks: This constructor sets up the initial state of the designer form, including initializing components and setting default values for properties. It also prepares the form for loading and designing reports by setting up necessary event handlers and UI elements.

member.name: M:GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.Advanced.DesignerForm.LoadReport(System.String)
member.summary: Loads a report from the specified file into the designer.
member.param: The full path to the report file that should be loaded.
member.remarks: This method attempts to open and load a report file into the designer for editing. Before loading the new report, it checks if there are any unsaved changes in the current session and prompts the user to save them. If the user cancels the save operation, the loading process is aborted to prevent loss of unsaved work. This method supports loading of report files compatible with the ActiveReports designer.

member.name: M:GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.Advanced.DesignerForm.GetDCEx(System.IntPtr,System.IntPtr,System.Int32)
member.summary: Retrieves a handle to a device context (DC) for the client area of a specified window or for the entire screen. You can use the returned handle in subsequent GDI functions to draw in the DC.
member.param: A handle to the window whose DC is to be retrieved. If this value is NULL, GetDCEx retrieves the DC for the entire screen.

A clipping region that may be combined with the visible region of the DC. If the value of flags is DCX_INTERSECTRGN or DCX_EXCLUDERGN, then the operating system assumes ownership of the region and will automatically delete it when it is no longer needed. Therefore, application should not reference the region after a successful call to GetDCEx using one of these flags. If hRgn is NULL, the clipping region is ignored.
Specifies how the DC is created. This parameter can be one or more of the DCX_ values.
member.returns: If the function succeeds, the return value is the handle to the DC for the specified window's client area. If the function fails, the return value is NULL.

remarks.para: After painting with a common DC, the ReleaseDC function must be called to release the DC. Class and private DCs do not have to be released. ReleaseDC must be called from the same thread that called GetDCEx. The number of DCs is limited only by available memory.
Note that the function is an imported function from the User32.dll library and is utilized within managed code through platform invocation services (P/Invoke).

member.name: M:GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.Advanced.ISessionSettingsStorage.Save(GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.Advanced.SessionSettings)
member.summary: Saves the specified session settings to persistent storage.
member.param: The instance containing the settings to be saved.
member.remarks: This method should serialize the object and write it to a storage medium in such a way that it can be retrieved later by the method. Implementations must handle any exceptions that may occur during the save operation, such as IO exceptions.

member.name: M:GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.Advanced.ISessionSettingsStorage.Load(GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.Advanced.SessionSettings)
member.summary: Loads session settings from persistent storage into the specified instance.

member.remarks: This method should read from the storage medium, deserialize the settings data, and populate the object with the retrieved values. Implementations must handle any exceptions that may occur during the load operation, such as IO exceptions or data format mismatches.

member.name: T:GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.Advanced.SessionSettings
member.summary: Represents the session settings for the Flat End-User Designer (FlatEUD) environment.

member.name: T:GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.Designer
member.summary: Serves as the central designer component for creating and editing reports, including both Section and Page within the ActiveReports designer environment.

remarks.para: The class is a key component of the ActiveReports design-time environment, facilitating the creation, editing, and previewing of report designs.
This class represents the windows forms component that could be used to integrate the report editing capabilities into a Windows forms application.

member.name: E:GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.Designer.ActiveTabChanged
member.summary: Occurs when the currently in the designer interface changes.
member.remarks: This event is triggered whenever the active tab within the designer's interface is switched, allowing for custom logic to be executed in response to this change. The property can be used within the event handler to determine the newly activated tab.

member.name: E:GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.Designer.ChartDataSourceClicked
member.summary: Occurs when a data source item within a chart is selected by the user.
member.remarks:
This event is raised in response to the user clicking on a data source item specifically for a chart component within the designer. It provides an opportunity to respond to the selection of a chart's data source, allowing for custom logic or UI to be invoked, such as displaying the data source properties or initiating data source configuration.
The parameter contains information about the clicked data source item, enabling detailed handling of the event.

member.name: E:GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.Designer.ContextMenuOpen
member.summary: Occurs immediately before the context menu is displayed in the designer.
member.remarks:
This event provides an opportunity to customize the context menu before it is shown to the user. You can add, remove, or modify menu items based on the current state of the designer or the selected elements within it.
Handlers for this event receive an argument of type , which provides information about the context menu and allows for its customization.

member.name: E:GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.Designer.DataSourceIconClick
member.summary: Occurs when the user clicks on the DataSource icon within the designer environment.
member.remarks:
This event is triggered as a direct response to the user's action of clicking the DataSource icon, typically used to initiate the process of connecting to or modifying the data source for the report being designed. It provides a hook for implementing custom behavior or displaying additional UI elements related to data source configuration.
Handlers attached to this event can access the event arguments to obtain context-specific information, enabling fine-grained control over the application's response to the event.

member.name: E:GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.Designer.DataSourceIconClicked
member.summary: Occurs after the DataSource dialog has been closed by the user.
member.remarks:
This event is fired following the closure of the DataSource dialog, which is typically used for configuring or selecting the data source for the report. It signifies that the user has completed their interaction with the DataSource dialog, allowing for post-dialog actions or updates to be initiated in response.
Event handlers can utilize this event to implement custom logic, such as refreshing data or UI elements based on the new or modified data source settings.

member.name: E:GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.Designer.DesignerTabChanged
member.summary: Occurs after the designer tab has been changed by the user.
member.remarks:
This event is fired when the user switches between different tabs in the designer interface, such as moving from the "Design" tab to the "Preview" tab. It allows for the execution of custom logic in response to this change, such as updating UI elements or performing cleanup tasks related to the tab change.
Event handlers can use this event to adapt the application's behavior to the newly active designer tab, enhancing the user experience and ensuring the application remains responsive to user actions.

member.name: E:GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.Designer.EditModeEntering
member.summary: Occurs just before the designer enters edit mode for a report component.
member.remarks:
This event provides an opportunity to intercept the action of entering edit mode. It can be used to implement custom logic before the designer allows editing of report component properties directly within the designer interface.
Listeners can use this event to, for example, validate conditions before editing is permitted or to prevent editing under certain circumstances by cancelling the edit mode transition.

member.name: E:GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.Designer.EditModeExit
member.summary: Occurs immediately after the designer exits edit mode for a report component.
member.remarks:
This event is triggered when the designer transitions out of edit mode, which could be due to the user completing their modifications or cancelling the edit operation. It provides an opportunity to execute custom logic after editing has concluded, such as validation, cleanup, or updating other parts of the UI in response to the changes made.
Listeners can use this event to perform actions that need to occur once editing is no longer active, ensuring that any necessary adjustments or checks are made following the edit session.

member.name: E:GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.Designer.LayoutChanged
member.summary: Occurs after the report layout has been modified. This event signifies a permanent change in the layout.
member.remarks:
This event is triggered once changes to the report's layout are finalized, such as after moving, adding, or deleting report elements. It serves as a notification that the layout has been altered in a way that cannot be undone without further actions by the user or programmatic interventions.
Event handlers can use this opportunity to perform tasks that need to occur after a layout change, such as updating UI elements, saving the report, or refreshing previews.

member.name: E:GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.Designer.LayoutChanging
member.summary: Occurs before a change in the layout is made. This event allows interception and prevention of layout modifications.
member.remarks:
This event provides a mechanism to monitor and potentially cancel changes to the report's layout before they are applied. It can be useful for enforcing constraints, validating changes, or implementing custom behavior in response to layout adjustments.
Handlers can inspect the event arguments to determine the nature of the proposed change and decide whether to allow it, modify it, or prevent it from occurring.

member.name: E:GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.Designer.LocateDataSource
member.summary: Occurs when a data source is needed for the report. This event enables dynamic data source resolution.
member.remarks:
This event is triggered when the report requires a data source that has not been predefined or needs to be resolved at runtime. It allows for the dynamic provision of data sources based on the report's requirements or user input.
Event handlers can use this opportunity to present data source selection dialogs, perform custom data source configuration, or apply logic to determine the appropriate data source for the current context.

member.name: E:GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.Designer.LocateCredentials
member.summary: Occurs when credentials are needed to access a data source. This event facilitates secure credential provision.
member.remarks:
This event is raised when accessing a data source requires authentication, and credentials are not available or need to be confirmed. It provides a secure way to request and apply credentials without hard-coding them into the report or application.
Handlers for this event can prompt the user for credentials, retrieve them from a secure store, or apply default credentials based on application logic.

member.name: E:GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.Designer.ReportChanged
member.summary: Occurs when any modification is made to the report, such as changes to the design, data sources, or properties.
member.remarks: This event is a broad notification that the report has been altered in some way. It can be triggered by a variety of actions, including but not limited to adding or removing report elements, modifying properties, or changing the report's data source. Handlers for this event can be used to implement functionality such as enabling save operations, refreshing previews, or updating UI elements to reflect the changes made to the report.

member.name: E:GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.Designer.SelectionChanged
member.summary: Occurs when the selection within the designer changes, such as when a different report component is selected by the user.
member.remarks: This event provides notification that the current selection within the designer has changed, which can occur through user interaction or programmatically. This is useful for updating property grids, toolbars, or other UI elements to reflect the properties and actions relevant to the newly selected components.

member.name: E:GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.Designer.ReportNameChanged
member.summary: Occurs when the name of the report changes. This event can be used to respond to changes in the report's name, such as updating UI elements or performing additional logic.

member.name: E:GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.Designer.ScriptChanged
member.summary: Occurs after modifications have been made to the report's script.
member.remarks: This event signals that changes have occurred to the script associated with the report. It is particularly useful for scenarios where the script is being edited directly within the designer or through an external editor integrated into the design environment. Handlers for this event can be used to compile the script, check for errors, or update UI elements to indicate the script's modified status.

member.name: E:GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.Designer.StatusChanged
member.summary: Occurs when there is a need to update toolbars or other UI elements related to Section reports, due to changes in the report's state or selection.
member.remarks: This event is raised in response to changes that affect the state or configuration of the report, necessitating updates to the UI. This could include changes to the selection, the report's data, or modifications to the design that require toolbars or other UI elements to be refreshed to accurately reflect the current context. Implementing handlers for this event allows for a dynamic and responsive design environment that adjusts to the user's actions and the report's state.

member.name: E:GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.Designer.ToolboxItemChanged
member.summary: Occurs when the property changes, indicating a modification to the toolbox item selection or properties.
member.remarks: This event is raised in response to changes in the toolbox item, such as when a new item is selected or an existing item's properties are modified. It provides an opportunity to execute custom logic in response to these changes, enabling dynamic updates to the UI or other components based on the current toolbox item state.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.Designer.ActiveTab
member.summary: Gets a value representing the currently selected tab in the designer interface.
member.value: The representing the active tab in the designer. This property provides access to the tab currently being interacted with by the user, allowing for context-specific operations based on the selected tab.
member.remarks: This property is particularly useful for determining the context within which the designer is operating, such as whether the user is focusing on design, preview, or Script. Accessing this property can help in tailoring the UI and functionality to better suit the needs of the current designer state.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.Designer.DrawGrid
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether a grid is displayed in the designer workspace.
member.value: true if the grid is displayed; otherwise, false. The default is false.
member.remarks: When set to true, a grid overlay appears in the designer, aiding in the alignment and precise placement of report elements.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.Designer.GridMode
member.summary: Gets or sets a value representing the mode in which the grid is displayed in the designer workspace.
member.value: The mode of the grid as defined by the enumeration. This determines how the grid lines are drawn in the designer, affecting the visual guidance provided for aligning and placing report elements.
member.remarks: The grid mode can be set to different styles such as dots or lines, depending on the user's preference or the specific requirements of the report design task at hand. Changing the grid mode can enhance the design experience by providing the appropriate level of visual guidance.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.Designer.FontResolver
member.summary: Gets or sets a value representing the font resolver used by the designer to resolve fonts in reports.
member.value: An that handles font resolution. The default is null, which indicates that the default font resolver is used.
member.remarks:
The font resolver is responsible for determining the specific font instance to use when rendering text in reports. This can be particularly useful in scenarios where custom fonts are used or when there is a need to map generic font names to specific font files. Implementing a custom allows for precise control over font selection and rendering in the designer environment.
Note: Setting this property to a custom font resolver overrides the default font resolution mechanism. Ensure that the custom resolver properly handles all font requests to avoid rendering issues.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.Designer.PageReportDesignerActions
member.summary: Gets or sets a value representing the allowed actions in PageReport Designer.
member.value: The page report designer actions as defined by the enumeration. The default value is .
member.remarks: This property controls the actions that are permitted within the PageReport Designer. It allows for granular control over the functionality available to the user, such as editing, deleting, or adding new pages to the report. By adjusting the allowed actions, the designer can be customized to fit specific user roles or workflows, enhancing security and usability.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.Designer.PropertyGrid
member.summary: Gets or sets a value representing the instance used by the designer to display and edit the properties of the currently selected report item.
member.value: The that is attached to the designer. This grid displays the properties of the report item currently selected in the designer, allowing the user to view and modify those properties.
member.remarks:
The property plays a crucial role in the report design process, providing a user-friendly interface for inspecting and editing the properties of report items. By integrating a into the designer, developers can offer end-users a powerful tool for customizing reports to meet their specific requirements.
This property is essential for enabling interactive report design experiences in applications that incorporate the GrapeCity ActiveReports Designer.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.Designer.ResourceLocator
member.summary: Gets or sets a value representing the mechanism for locating and retrieving report resources such as images, data sources, and subreports.
member.value: An instance of that is responsible for locating and retrieving resources needed by the report. If not set, the designer uses a default implementation.
member.remarks:
The plays a critical role in the report generation process by enabling dynamic resolution of resources at design time and runtime. This property allows for customization of the resource resolution process, which can be essential for applications that store report resources in non-standard locations or need to apply custom logic to resource retrieval.
Setting this property to a custom implementation can provide greater flexibility and control over how resources are located and loaded, thereby accommodating complex application scenarios and resource management strategies.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.Designer.ReportPartsDirectory
member.summary: Gets or sets a value representing the directory path where report parts are stored for use in the report items library.
member.value: The directory path for report parts.
member.remarks: This property specifies the location from which report parts are loaded into the report items library. Report parts can include reusable report components, templates, or other resources that enhance report design efficiency. By default, this path is set to the current user's Documents folder, but it can be customized to point to any accessible directory containing the desired report parts.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.Designer.ScrollingMode
member.summary: Gets or sets a value representing the scrolling mode for the designer view.
member.value: The scrolling modes as defined by the enumeration.
member.remarks: The default value is ScrollingMode.Continuous, which allows for smooth scrolling through the designer. This property can be set to ScrollingMode.Paged to restrict the view to a single page at a time, enhancing the focus on individual report sections during design.

example.code: // Set the designer to use paged scrolling mode. designer.ScrollingMode = ScrollingMode.Paged;

member.name: P:GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.Designer.Selection
member.summary: Gets a value representing the collection of objects currently selected in the designer.
member.value: A object representing the current selection within the designer. This collection includes all report elements or components that the user has selected.
member.remarks: This property is essential for operations that need to act on the user's selection, such as property editing, deletion, or manipulation of report elements. It provides a way to programmatically access and interact with the selected items in the designer.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.Designer.ShowDataSourceIcon
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the DataSource icon is visible on the detail section bar. This icon allows users to modify the report's data source settings.
member.value: true if the DataSource icon is visible; otherwise, false. The default is determined by the initial configuration of the designer settings.
member.remarks:
Displaying the DataSource icon provides a convenient way for users to access and modify the data source settings directly from the report designer interface. This property can be used to control the visibility of the DataSource icon based on the specific requirements or permissions of the application.
When set to true, the DataSource icon appears on the detail section bar, offering users a quick way to access data source configuration options. Setting this property to false hides the icon, which may be useful in scenarios where data source settings are predetermined or should not be modified by the user.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.Designer.Toolbox
member.summary: Gets or sets a value representing the implementation for the report designer.
member.value: An instance of that provides access to the toolbox service used by the report designer.
member.remarks:
The toolbox service is a key component in the report designer that manages the toolbox items, such as controls and components, which can be dragged onto the report design surface. This property allows for the customization or replacement of the toolbox service, enabling advanced scenarios such as dynamically changing the available toolbox items based on certain conditions.
Note: Setting this property with a custom implementation of can significantly alter the behavior and capabilities of the report designer's toolbox. It should be done with understanding of the underlying mechanics and implications.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.Designer.ToolPanel
member.summary: Gets or sets a value representing the tools that are available in the designer's tool panel.
member.value: A value that specifies the buttons displayed in the tool panel. The default is , which displays all available tools.
member.remarks:
The tool panel provides quick access to various actions and settings within the designer. This property allows for customization of the tool panel by specifying which buttons should be available. For example, you can limit the tool panel to only show zoom controls or the grid toggle button, depending on the needs of your application.
Use the enumeration to configure the available tools. This can enhance the user interface by simplifying the tool panel based on the context of the task being performed.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.Designer.UndoManager
member.summary: Gets a value representing the instance that manages undo and redo operations within the designer.
member.value: The that allows for the undoing and redoing of changes made in the designer.
member.remarks:
The is a critical component of the designer's user experience, providing users with the ability to reverse actions or restore them if reversed unintentionally. This property exposes the undo manager associated with the current instance of the designer, enabling programmatic access to its functionality.
Through the , developers can programmatically trigger undo or redo operations, check the availability of such operations, and even integrate more complex undo/redo scenarios into their applications.

member.name: T:GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.DesignerAction
member.summary: Enumerates the available designer commands (actions) that can be executed within the ActiveReports designer environment.
member.remarks:
The enumeration provides a comprehensive list of actions that can be performed by the user or programmatically within the ActiveReports designer. These actions cover a wide range of functionalities, including file operations, editing, formatting, alignment, and more, to facilitate a rich design experience.
Actions include operations like opening and saving files, cutting, copying, pasting, undoing, redoing, and deleting elements, as well as more specific design tasks such as aligning objects, setting font properties, managing borders, and working with data sources.
This enumeration allows for the implementation of a dynamic and user-friendly interface in the ActiveReports designer, enabling users to efficiently create and modify reports.

member.name: T:GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.LayoutMode
member.summary: Represents the layout modes available in the ActiveReports designer, specifying how elements align and snap within the design surface.
member.remarks:
The enumeration allows for the customization of the design surface behavior in the ActiveReports designer. Users can enable or combine different layout modes to facilitate precise placement and alignment of report elements.
Available modes include:
for no snapping or alignment aids,
to enable snapping to a grid pattern,
to enable snapping to alignment lines based on the positions of other elements,
to make helper lines less prominent, aiding in design without distraction.
This enumeration supports a bitwise combination of its member values, allowing multiple layout modes to be active simultaneously for enhanced design flexibility.

member.name: F:GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.LayoutMode.None
member.summary: Represents the layout mode which disables all snapping and alignment aids on the design surface.

member.name: F:GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.LayoutMode.SnapGrid
member.summary: Represents the layout mode which enables snapping to grid lines on the design surface.

member.name: F:GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.LayoutMode.SnapLines
member.summary: Represents the layout mode which enables snapping of elements to alignment lines based on the positions of other elements on the design surface.

member.name: F:GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.LayoutMode.DimHelperLines
member.summary: Represents the layout mode which makes helper lines less prominent, aiding in design without distraction.

member.name: T:GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.MouseMode
member.summary: Represents the mouse interaction modes available within the ActiveReports designer.
member.remarks: This enumeration allows for the specification of how mouse actions are interpreted in the designer environment. It supports modes for selecting components and panning across the design surface, providing flexibility in user interaction.

member.name: F:GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.MouseMode.Select
member.summary: Represents the mouse mode that allows selecting and manipulating design components.
member.remarks: In this mode, clicking and dragging with the mouse selects components. Additional actions, such as resizing and moving, can be performed on selected components.

member.name: F:GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.MouseMode.Pan
member.summary: Represents the mouse mode that allows panning the view of the design surface.
member.remarks: In this mode, clicking and dragging with the mouse moves the view of the design surface, allowing the user to navigate large reports or designs without using scroll bars.

member.name: T:GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.Selection
member.summary: Represents a collection of selected components within the ActiveReports designer environment.
member.remarks: This class provides functionality to manage the selection of components in the designer. It allows querying the current selection, changing the selection, and listening for selection changes. The selection can include controls, sections, or other design-time components. This class is particularly useful for extending the designer's functionality or integrating with other parts of the application that need to react to changes in the designer's selection state.

member.name: M:GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.Selection.#ctor(System.ComponentModel.Design.ISelectionService)
member.summary: Constructs a new instance using the provided selection service.
member.param: An that manages component selection within the designer.
member.exception: Thrown if is null, indicating that a valid selection service is required.
member.remarks: This constructor initializes the object with a selection service, which is essential for managing the selection of components in the designer environment. The selection service allows for operations such as querying and modifying the current selection of components.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.Selection.IsSynchronized
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether access to the collection is synchronized (thread safe).
member.value: Always returns false, as the selection collection is not thread-safe. Access to the collection should be managed carefully in multi-threaded scenarios to avoid concurrency issues.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.Selection.Count
member.summary: Gets the number of components currently selected in the designer.
member.value: The count of selected components. This includes controls, sections, and other design-time components that are currently selected within the ActiveReports designer environment.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.Selection.Item(System.Int32)
member.summary: Retrieves the selected component at the specified index within the collection.
member.param: The zero-based index of the component to retrieve.
member.returns: The component at the specified index. If the index is out of range, this will throw an .
member.exception: Thrown when the is outside the bounds of the collection.
member.remarks: This indexer provides direct access to a specific component within the selection. It is useful for iterating over the selected components or accessing a component at a specific position.

member.name: M:GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.Selection.Select(System.Object)
member.summary: Replaces the current selection with the specified object.
member.param: The object to select. This becomes the only selected object in the designer.
member.remarks: This method changes the current selection to the specified object, effectively deselecting any previously selected objects. It is equivalent to setting the selection with , which means the new selection replaces the old one entirely.

member.name: M:GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.Selection.Select(System.Object,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Adds the specified object to the current selection or makes it the primary selection.
member.param: The object to add to the selection or make primary.
If true, adds the object to the current selection. If false, makes the object the only selected item.
member.remarks: This method modifies the current selection based on the value of . If is true, the specified object is added to the current selection, maintaining any existing selections. If is false, the current selection is replaced with the specified object, making it the primary selection. This behavior aligns with the selection type.

member.name: M:GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.Selection.Clear
member.summary: Clears all selections within the designer.
member.remarks: This method clears the current selection, effectively deselecting any components that were previously selected.

member.name: M:GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.Selection.CopyTo(System.Array,System.Int32)
member.summary: Copies the elements of the current selection into an array, starting at a particular array index.
member.param: The one-dimensional array that is the destination of the elements copied from the current selection. The array must have zero-based indexing.
The zero-based index in at which copying begins.
member.remarks: This method is used to copy the currently selected components within the designer environment to a specified array, starting at a particular index. It is useful for operations that require processing or manipulation of the selected components outside the context of the selection service. The method ensures that the elements are copied in a manner that respects the order in which they are currently selected.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.Selection.SyncRoot
member.summary: Gets an object that can be used to synchronize access to the collection.
member.value: Always returns null, as this collection does not support synchronization. Access to the collection is not thread-safe.
member.remarks: This property is intended to provide compatibility with the ICollection interface. However, because the selection collection is inherently not thread-safe, this property does not return a valid synchronization object. Consumers of this class should ensure that access to the collection is properly synchronized in multi-threaded scenarios.

member.name: M:GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.Selection.GetEnumerator
member.summary: Returns an enumerator that iterates through the collection of selected components.
member.returns: An object that can be used to iterate through the collection.
member.remarks: This method provides an enumerator for the collection of components currently selected in the ActiveReports designer environment. It allows for enumeration over the selected components, enabling operations such as iteration and inspection of the selection set. This can be particularly useful for extensions or functionalities that need to interact with or modify the set of selected components in the designer.

member.name: T:GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.UndoManager
member.summary: Manages undo and redo operations for the ActiveReports designer.

remarks.para: The class encapsulates the functionality required to manage a history of operations performed in the ActiveReports designer, allowing users to undo and redo actions. This class interacts with an underlying undo engine to track changes and manage the undo/redo stack.

It provides methods to perform undo and redo operations, query the count of operations available for undo and redo, and retrieve descriptions of these operations for display in a user interface. The class also supports clearing the undo/redo history and raises events to notify subscribers when changes occur in the history.
This class implements the interface to properly release resources associated with the undo engine.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.UndoManager.UndoCount
member.summary: Gets the number of actions currently stored in the undo stack.
member.value: The count of undoable actions. This value can be used to determine if undo operations are available.

member.name: P:GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.UndoManager.RedoCount
member.summary: Gets the number of actions currently available in the redo stack.
member.value: The count of redoable actions. This value indicates how many operations can be redone.

member.name: E:GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.UndoManager.Changed
member.summary: Occurs when a change is made to the undo or redo stack, indicating that the state of the report has changed.
member.remarks: This event is raised after an undo or redo operation is performed, as well as after the undo/redo history is cleared. It can be used to update UI elements or perform other actions in response to changes in the report's state.

member.name: M:GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.UndoManager.Undo
member.summary: Reverses the most recent operation in the undo stack.
member.remarks: This method reverts the last action that was recorded in the undo stack, effectively "undoing" the most recent change made by the user. After the operation is undone, it is moved to the redo stack, allowing it to be redone if necessary. The event is raised to notify subscribers that the state of the undo/redo history has changed.

member.name: M:GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.UndoManager.Redo
member.summary: Reapplies the most recently undone operation from the redo stack.
member.remarks: This method reapplies the last action that was undone, effectively "redoing" the most recent change that was reversed. After the operation is redone, it is moved back to the undo stack, allowing it to be undone again if necessary. The event is raised to notify subscribers that the state of the undo/redo history has changed.

member.name: M:GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.UndoManager.Clear
member.summary: Empties both the undo and redo stacks, effectively resetting the history.
member.remarks: This method clears all recorded operations from both the undo and redo stacks. It is useful when the state of the document changes in such a way that previous operations are no longer relevant or applicable. After clearing the history, the event is raised to notify subscribers that the undo/redo history has been reset. Additionally, if any subscribers are registered to the event, it is also raised to signal a complete reset of the undo/redo system.

member.name: M:GrapeCity.ActiveReports.Design.UndoManager.UndoDescription(System.Int32)
member.summary: Retrieves a description of the specified undo action in a human-readable format.
member.param: The zero-based index of the undo action for which to retrieve the description. Index 0 corresponds to the oldest action in the undo stack.
member.returns: A string containing the description of the specified undo action.
member.remarks: This method translates the index provided to match the internal representation used by the undo engine, where the last operation (the most recent one) has an index of 0.
